cards.text: For chapters now, the writer of Chronicles has been listing the families of every tribe, and here he wraps it up: all Israel was recorded in the genealogies written in the Book of the Kings of Israel. Then he gives the hard news. Judah was carried off into exile.

cards.question: Judah is carried off into exile. Where to?
The writer tells us why. Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their ___.

cards.text: But the story doesn't end in Babylon. People are moving back onto their own property in their cities, and somebody has to be first through the door.

cards.question: Who are the first to resettle their own property in their cities?

answers.text: Israelites priests Levites and temple servants
Kings princes and the royal guards

cards.question: Some of the returning people settle right in Jerusalem. True or false: every one of them comes from the tribe of Judah.

cards.text: Then comes the roll call of who moved in: family heads from Judah and Benjamin, then the priests, then the Levites. The Benjamites bring 956 relatives, and the priests bring 1,760, all able men for serving in the house of God.

Next up, the gatekeepers: Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman and their relatives, with Shallum as their chief. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer, and I would have PAID for a gatekeeper deciding what got tossed in on top of me.

cards.question: Before this, Shallum the chief gatekeeper was stationed at which gate?

cards.text: Shallum is a Korahite, and he and his Korahite relatives are assigned to guard the thresholds of the Tent. Standing in a doorway as a holy calling? I bet no bouncer in history ever took a door that seriously.

cards.question: True or false: the Korahites are the first in their family ever assigned to guard the dwelling of the LORD.

cards.text: Then the writer looks way back. In earlier times, the man in charge of the gatekeepers was Phinehas son of Eleazar, Aaron's grandson (Exodus 6:25).

cards.question: In earlier times Phinehas was in charge of the gatekeepers, and the ___ was with him.
True or false: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah is the gatekeeper at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.

cards.text: All told, 212 men are chosen to be gatekeepers at the thresholds, registered by genealogy in their villages. And these aren't jobs you grab off a sign-up sheet by the break room, friend.

cards.question: Who appointed the gatekeepers to their positions of trust?

cards.text: So the gatekeepers and their descendants are assigned to guard the gates of the house of the LORD, the house called the Tent. Generations of door duty. That family reunion has the BEST security in town.

cards.question: True or false: the gatekeepers are stationed only on the east side of the house of the LORD.

cards.text: That's a lot of gates to cover. So their relatives come in from their villages at fixed times to serve alongside them.

cards.question: The relatives from the villages come to serve with the gatekeepers for periods of ___ days.

cards.text: But the four chief gatekeepers, who are Levites, get something even bigger to watch over.

cards.question: What are the four chief gatekeepers entrusted with in the house of God?

cards.text: They spend the night stationed all around the house of God, because guarding it is their job. Overnight shift, every night. And then the sun comes up.

cards.question: Every morning the chief gatekeepers are responsible for ___ the house of God.

cards.text: Opening up EVERY morning, friend, and nobody hits snooze when they're holding the keys to the house of God. Some of them are also in charge of the articles used in worship.

cards.question: What do they do with the worship articles whenever they're brought in or taken out?

cards.text: Others are in charge of the furnishings and other articles of the sanctuary, plus the fine flour, wine, oil, frankincense and spices. Flour on the list? Oh, now we're TALKING.

cards.question: True or false: some of the sons of the priests are the ones who mix the spices.

cards.text: Hold on, friend, I need a second, because this next job is the one I was MADE for. A Levite named Mattithiah, the firstborn son of Shallum the Korahite, gets it.

cards.question: What job is Mattithiah entrusted with?
Some of their Kohathite relatives are responsible for preparing the rows of the ___ every ___.

cards.text: Then there are the musicians, heads of Levite families who stay in the temple chambers. And they're excused from every other duty.

cards.question: Why are the musicians exempt from other duties?

answers.text: They are on duty day and night
Their families serve in their place

cards.question: True or false: all these heads of Levite families, chiefs according to their genealogies, live in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Then the writer lists one more family, the family of Jeiel the father of Gibeon, and a big name shows up: Kish was the father of Saul, the man who became Israel's first king (1 Samuel 11:15). From Saul's son Jonathan, the line runs all the way down to Azel and his six sons.

findings.problem: The card says the earlier chapters list the families of every tribe. 1 Chronicles 1-8 has no genealogy for Dan or Zebulun, so that is not accurate. It is also a fact from outside the passage, and the card gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This true or false card about Zechariah son of Meshelemiah comes straight after another choice card, and no card tells its setup. Zechariah has not come up before, so the baker can only guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Most of the choice cards in stop 1 are discovery questions the baker cannot reason out from earlier cards. These are cards 6 (which tribes), 9 (which gate), 11 (whether their fathers guarded too), 14 (Zechariah) and 16 (who appointed the gatekeepers). Card 2 is also mostly discovery. Only a few cards, such as 3 and 13, are informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: This true or false card about the sons of the priests mixing the spices has no setup. Card 11 only lists spices among the supplies. Nothing points the baker toward who mixes them, so the pick is a coin flip.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card says the relatives come from the villages because there are a lot of gates to cover. It opens with 'That's a lot of gates to cover. So...' But 1 Chronicles 9:25 does not say why the relatives come.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: Almost all of 1 Chronicles 9 is name lists, counts and duty rosters. Verses 17-34 list gatekeeper and Levite duties, which looks like 'mostly detail and not much happens.' If all of that counted as a long stretch, the passage would have almost nothing left for choice cards. The walkthrough instead treats verses 17-34 as story moments and gives them 17 choice cards.
findings.question: When a whole passage is mostly long-stretch material, like the duty roster in 1 Chronicles 9:17-34, should those duties get choice cards as story moments, or should they be summed up as long stretches? If they are summed up, the passage would be left with very few or no choice cards. How should it be handled then?
